Nom sous lequel circule un immense corpu: Name under which a vast body of Arabic alchemy circulated.
Médecin et alchimiste persan. Il classe: Persian physician and alchemist. He classified substances and told smallpox from measles.
Lettré taoïste. Son Baopuzi décrit les é: Daoist scholar. His Baopuzi described elixirs of immortality.
Médecin suisse. Il veut que l'alchimie f: Swiss physician. He wanted alchemy to make remedies rather than gold.
Savant irlandais. The Sceptical Chymist: Irish scientist. The Sceptical Chymist (1661) demanded experiments, not dogma.
Chimiste anglais. Chaque élément, dit-il: English chemist. Each element, he said, is made of atoms of its own weight.
Chimiste suédois. Il invente la dynamite: Swedish chemist. He invented dynamite and left his fortune to the Nobel Prizes.
Chimiste allemand, principal auteur de l: German chemist, principal author of the theory of chemical structure. In 1865, he proposed that the six carbon atoms of benzene form a ring.
Chimiste français. En 1912, il décrit la: French chemist. In 1912, he described the reaction between sugars and amino acids that browns bread, meat and coffee.
Parfumeuse d'Assur, en Mésopotamie, à la: Perfumer of Assur, in Mesopotamia, head of the royal palace's perfumers. A cuneiform tablet shows her distilling and filtering flowers, oils and resins: one of the earliest chemists known by name.
Alchimiste d'Alexandrie, connue par Zosi: Alchemist of Alexandria, known through Zosimos who quotes her. She is credited with the bain-marie and the kerotakis, and with the first description of a three-armed still.
Alchimiste né à Panopolis, en Égypte. Se: Alchemist born in Panopolis, Egypt. His books are the oldest known writings on alchemy; in them, alchemy transforms the soul as much as matter.
